subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Filling/emptying rates, LCM method, leak-induced delay, combined operation

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B fills the same tank in 8 hours. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Rate of A = 1/12 tank per hour. Rate of B = 1/8 per hour. Combined = 1/12 + 1/8 = 2/24 + 3/24 = 5/24 per hour. Time = reciprocal = 24/5 = 4.8 hours. LCM shortcut: take LCM(12, 8) = 24 units (tank capacity). A fills 24/12 = 2 u/hr; B fills 24/8 = 3 u/hr; together 5 u/hr → 24/5 = 4.8 h.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B empties the full tank in 9 hours. If both pipes are opened together on an empty tank, the tank will be filled in:

options.option_text: Never (B drains faster than A fills)

questions.explanation: Rate of A = +1/6 (filling). Rate of B = −1/9 (emptying). Net = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18 per hour. Time = 18 hours. Shortcut with LCM: capacity = 18 u. A: +3 u/hr, B: −2 u/hr → net +1 u/hr → 18 hrs. Since A is faster than B, the tank does fill — just slowly.

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B, C can fill a tank in 10, 15 and 30 hours respectively. If all three are opened together, time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 + 1/30. LCM(10,15,30) = 30. Rates in 30-unit tank: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1 → 6 u/hr combined → 30/6 = 5 hours. Same in fractions: 3/30 + 2/30 + 1/30 = 6/30 = 1/5 → 5 hours.

questions.stem: A tank with a leak empties a full tank in 8 hours. An inlet pipe fills water at the rate of 6 litres/minute. When both the inlet and the leak are open together, the tank is emptied in 12 hours. The capacity of the tank (in litres) is:
questions.explanation: Let capacity = V litres. Leak rate = V/8 per hour (emptying). Inlet = 6 L/min = 360 L/hr (filling). Net emptying rate with both open = V/12 per hour. So V/8 − 360 = V/12. Multiply by 24: 3V − 8640 = 2V → V = 8640 litres. Check: leak rate = 1080 L/hr; inlet = 360 L/hr; net empty 720 L/hr → 8640/720 = 12 h ✓.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe A alone takes 5 hours less than pipe B. How long does pipe B take alone to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Let B take x hours alone; then A takes (x − 5). Rate A + Rate B = 1/6. 1/(x−5) + 1/x = 1/6. Combine: (x + x − 5) / [x(x−5)] = 1/6 → 6(2x − 5) = x² − 5x → 12x − 30 = x² − 5x → x² − 17x + 30 = 0. Using quadratic formula: x = (17 ± √(289 − 120))/2 = (17 ± 13)/2 → x = 15 or x = 2. x = 2 fails (x − 5 negative). So B = 15 h, A = 10 h. Verify: 1/15 + 1/10 = 2/30 + 3/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 ✓.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 20 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom it now takes 25 hours to fill. How long would the leak alone empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: Rate of A = 1/20. Combined rate (A filling + leak emptying) = 1/25. Leak rate = 1/20 − 1/25 = 5/100 − 4/100 = 1/100 per hour (emptying). So the leak alone empties a full tank in 100 hours. Classic formula: if filling time without leak = t₁ and with leak = t₂, leak-alone time = (t₁ × t₂) / (t₂ − t₁) = (20 × 25) / 5 = 100.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours. Pipe B fills the same tank in 15 hours. Both are opened together but A is closed after 3 hours. How many more hours will B alone need to finish filling?
questions.explanation: In the first 3 hours, A fills 3/10 and B fills 3/15 = 1/5. Together = 3/10 + 2/10 = 5/10 = 1/2 of the tank. Remaining = 1/2 tank. B's rate = 1/15 per hour → time to fill remaining 1/2 = (1/2) ÷ (1/15) = 15/2 = 7.5 hours. LCM check: capacity 30 u; A = 3, B = 2. First 3 hours: 3·3 + 3·2 = 9 + 6 = 15 u done; 15 u left; B alone at 2 u/hr → 15/2 = 7.5 h ✓.
